question.text: A 2 kg block and a 1 kg block rest on a smooth horizontal surface, joined by a string AB of mass 1 kg, with end A attached to the 2 kg block and end B attached to the 1 kg block. A horizontal force F of 8 N pulls the 1 kg block away from the 2 kg block. Find the string tension at end A and the string tension at end B.
conditions: string AB has mass 1 kg (not massless)
end A of string attached to the 2 kg block, end B attached to the 1 kg block
F = 8 N applied horizontally on the 1 kg block, pulling it away from the 2 kg block

figure.description: On a horizontal frictionless surface: a 2 kg block on the left connected by string end A to string end B on a 1 kg block to its right; the force F = 8 N acts horizontally on the 1 kg block, pointing further right (away from the 2 kg block).

solution.approach: Find the common acceleration of the whole three-part system, then apply Newton's second law to each end block to get the tension at each end of the string.

steps.text: Find the acceleration of the whole system: the two blocks plus the string.
Apply Newton's second law to the 2 kg block alone; only the tension at A pulls it.
Apply Newton's second law to the 1 kg block alone; F pulls it forward and the tension at B pulls it back.

common_mistakes.text: Treating the string as massless makes the tension equal at both ends, giving a = 8/3 m/s² and one tension of 5.33 N instead of the two different values 4 N and 6 N.
